title: A finite birational morphism to a normal integral scheme is an isomorphism
statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be integral schemes [def-pc-integral-scheme], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] inducing an isomorphism $k(Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}k(X)$ of function fields [def-sc-function-field]. Assume every local ring of $Y$ is a normal domain in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Then $f$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0AB1 (lemma-finite-birational-over-normal): on affine opens, the finite birational ring inclusion identifies the two fraction fields, and integrally closedness of the normal target forces equality.

proof.text: Let $\xi$ and $\eta$ be the generic points of $X$ and $Y$. That $f$ induces a map $k(Y)=\mathcal O_{Y,\eta}\to\mathcal O_{X,\xi}=k(X)$ means $f(\xi)=\eta$, and the induced map is the stalk map $f^\sharp_\xi$, which is the given isomorphism. Let $V\subseteq Y$ be any nonempty affine open, $A=\mathcal O_Y(V)$. Because $f$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], $U=f^{-1}(V)$ is affine, $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B=\mathcal O_X(U)$, and $f^\sharp:A\to B$ is finite; $U$ is nonempty since $\xi\in U$ ($f(\xi)=\eta\in V$). By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] (applied to $Y,V$ and to $X,U$) $A$ and $B$ are domains and the germ maps $A\to k(Y)$, $B\to k(X)$ are injective and make $k(Y)$, $k(X)$ fraction fields of $A$, $B$. Compatibility of germs with $f^\sharp$ gives a commutative square: $A\to B\to k(X)$ equals $A\to k(Y)\xrightarrow{f^\sharp_\xi}k(X)$. The second composite is injective, so $A\to B$ is injective; identifying everything inside $K:=k(X)$ via these injections, $A\subseteq B\subseteq K$ and $K$ is the fraction field of both $A$ and $B$.

source.place: Tag 0AB1, proof first paragraph: finite morphisms are affine on affine opens and birationality gives an injective map with isomorphic fraction fields.

proof.text: $A$ is a normal domain. Indeed $A$ is a domain (Step 1). For a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset A$ let $y\in V$ be the corresponding point; by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization](c) the germ map identifies $A_{\mathfrak m}$ with $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ as rings, which is a normal domain by hypothesis [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. So every $A_{\mathfrak m}$ is a normal domain, and [lem-weil-pbc-normal-domain-of-local-normal] (Stacks 030B, (3)$\Rightarrow$(1)) shows that $A$ is integrally closed in its fraction field $K$. Since $A\to B$ is finite, every $b\in B$ is integral over $A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. As $b\in K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ and $A$ is integrally closed in $K$, $b\in A$. Hence $A\to B$ is surjective, so (being injective) an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0AB1, proof: 'As Y is normal, the ring O_Y(V) is integrally closed in the fraction field. Since f is finite (or integral) every element of O_X(U) is integral over O_Y(V). We conclude O_Y(V)=O_X(U).' Normality of O_Y(V) as in properties.tex Tag 033L (lemma-integral-normal), whose proof is algebra.tex Tag 030B (lemma-normality-is-local).

proof.text: Over each nonempty affine open $V\subseteq Y$ the restriction $f^{-1}(V)\to V$ is a morphism of affine schemes $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ whose ring map $A\to B$ is an isomorphism by Step 2, so it is an isomorphism; over the empty open $f^{-1}(\emptyset)=\emptyset$. The affine opens cover $Y$, and being an isomorphism is local on the target (the restrictions are bijective homeomorphisms on a cover, hence $f$ is a homeomorphism, and $f^\sharp$ is an isomorphism on stalks). Hence $f$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0AB1, final sentence: equality on affine opens proves that $f$ is an isomorphism.
